boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Missouri-Columbia, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daylight-to-evening, under-21-safe sequence for learning Mizzou’s core campus places and nearby outdoor options.

cards.title: Start at Francis Quadrangle
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · central campus
cards.notes: Begin by walking the quad and using the University Archives page to recognize the setting and the historic Columns before moving through campus.
cards.short_summary: A campus-orientation stop anchored by Mizzou’s historic quad.
cards.evidence_claim: University Archives identifies Francis Quadrangle and the Columns as the remains of Academic Hall, Mizzou’s first campus building.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; use the campus map for current routes and accessibility information.

cards.title: Pause at the Columns
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · Francis Quadrangle
cards.notes: Take a close look at the limestone Columns from the quad, then continue toward Jesse Hall; keep this as a short landmark stop, not a climb.
cards.short_summary: A focused look at the surviving Columns of Academic Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou states that the Columns originally provided structural support for Academic Hall, its first campus building.
cards.access_notes: View from the surrounding quadrangle; follow posted campus-area rules.

cards.title: Find Jesse Hall’s dome
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · Lowry Mall edge
cards.notes: Use Jesse Hall as a visual waypoint while crossing the central campus. If you enter for an event, confirm its access details with the event host.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable administrative building beside the campus core.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou describes Jesse Hall as its domed administration building with meeting and event spaces and an indoor auditorium.
cards.access_notes: Building rooms and events may have separate access arrangements.

cards.title: Walk through Memorial Union
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 518 Hitt Street
cards.notes: Enter through an open public entrance and take in the archway and tower. Keep voices low beneath the arches in keeping with the documented custom.
cards.short_summary: A campus community center with a memorial tradition in its archway.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou says Memorial Union serves as a student gathering place and memorial; students customarily whisper and tip hats beneath the tower.
cards.access_notes: Located at 518 Hitt St.; accessible entrances and elevators are documented on the Union’s visit page.

cards.title: Settle into Ellis Library
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · 520 S. 9th Street
cards.notes: Choose an individual or group study area for a calm reset, and check the library’s current hours before planning a late-evening return.
cards.short_summary: Mizzou’s main library, with spaces for solo and group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou Libraries identifies Ellis as the main library for most undergraduates and says it has individual and group study spaces.
cards.access_notes: The library page lists regular access from Sunday 10 a.m. through Friday 7 p.m., plus Saturday 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; verify current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Browse the museum galleries
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · Ellis Library east wing
cards.notes: Enter through the museum’s Lowry Mall or accessible Hitt Street entrance, browse at your pace, and leave food, drinks, flash photography, and backpacks outside.
cards.short_summary: A free art-and-archaeology museum inside Ellis Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Art & Archaeology is in Ellis Library’s east wing, is open to the community, and always has free admission.
cards.source_title: Visit & Tours — Museum of Art and Archaeology
cards.access_notes: Regular gallery hours are Tuesday–Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday noon–4 p.m.; closed on University observed holidays.

cards.title: Take a quiet loop in Peace Park
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · north edge of campus
cards.notes: Walk across McAlester Bridge, choose a bench for a short pause, and stay on established paths while taking in this wooded campus setting.
cards.short_summary: A wooded campus park with benches and McAlester Bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou describes Peace Park as a four-acre, wooded area on the northern edge of campus with McAlester Bridge and park benches.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus destination; use the campus map and follow posted conditions.

cards.title: Use the MU Student Center as a reset
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · campus community center
cards.notes: Stop by to orient yourself to campus services, relax with friends, or check what programming is posted; confirm individual venue access at the building.
cards.short_summary: One of Mizzou’s two student-union community centers.
cards.evidence_claim: Missouri Student Unions says the MU Student Center and Memorial Student Union serve as campus community centers with services, study, food and programming.
cards.access_notes: Specific services, food venues and events can have separate schedules or access requirements.

cards.title: Walk the MizzouRec Trail
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · campus connection to MKT
cards.notes: Choose a comfortable out-and-back stretch in daylight, bring water, and use the trail as a low-key connection between campus and Columbia’s larger trail network.
cards.short_summary: A 1.5-mile campus trail that connects to Columbia’s MKT system.
cards.evidence_claim: MizzouRec describes the MizzouRec Trail as a 1.5-mile trail connecting campus to Columbia’s MKT and trail system.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor route; check weather, daylight and current trail conditions before setting out.

cards.title: Finish at Stankowski Field
cards.subtitle: Sunday daytime · 1000 Rollins Street area
cards.notes: End the weekend with a daylight walk or run on the track, then head back to campus; confirm any field restrictions before using athletic surfaces.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor recreation area with a track and synthetic-turf fields.
cards.evidence_claim: MizzouRec says Stankowski Field has a one-third-mile track and three synthetic-turf fields and is open from dawn until 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: MizzouRec lists Stankowski Field as open from dawn until 11 p.m.; follow posted field-use rules and current notices.
